contexts.text: The fourth state is when he is... illuminated with faith.
The illumination of the gentiles. Treated of.
Jonathan... said that his eyes... were illuminated ().
That the external man is illuminated by the internal. Signified.
To lift up the eyes and see = to be illuminated, and to perceive.
Paran = illumination from the Lord's Divine Human.
Resplendence and light = illumination.
The obscurity (of the spiritual man) is illuminated by the Lord's Divine Human. Treated of. AC 2716. AC 2718.
From this illumination there comes forth in his Rational the affection of truth; and in his Natural the affection of knowledges.
(Thus) the Lord, from the Divine Human, can illuminate minds even more remote from the celestial things of love...
The light of Heaven is such, that when it illuminates the sight of Spirits and Angels, it also at the same time illuminates their understanding...
It is the Lord's Divine Human which illuminates both the sight and the understanding of the spiritual...
His Intellectual is illuminated. Signified, Explained.
The Natural is then illuminated from the interior...
The general influx of truth is the illumination which gives the faculty of apperceiving and understanding truth. This illumination is from the light of Heaven...

He who would have perception in spiritual things must be in the affection of truth from good; and must continually long to know truths. Hence his Intellectual is illuminated; and when the Intellectual is illuminated, it is given to him to perceive something inwardly in himself.

In order that the eye may see, it is necessary that there be light which may illumine it... So... it is necessary that the light of Heaven... should illumine (the intellectual mind); and when this (internal) eye is illuminated by that light, it then sees the things which are around it... But when this light does not illumine it... it sees nothing... The light which illumines the intellectual mind is truly light.
When spiritual good is in illumination from such influx...
Good is like a flame... and when it meets any truth, it not only illuminates it, but also introduces it into its own light...

The (intellectual) light itself has been perceived as an illumination, which enlightened the substances of the interior sight... This general illumination causes the objects of the things to appear; as do the objects of the Earth to an illumined eye...
Generals are infilled with particulars; and these with singulars; thus with new truths, from which the illumination increases.
Hence it is that they are illuminated and clever in the things of the work; but dimmed and dull in the things of Heaven.
These believe themselves to be illuminated when they have confirmed with themselves the doctrinal things of the Church...

The right eye corresponds to the intellectual sight not only in so far as it is illuminated by truth, but also in so far as it is illuminated by good. Thus does the Lord look at man from good; and illuminate him through good.
And by night in a pillar of fire to illuminate them () = that when there is a state of obscurity it is tempered by means of illustration by good.
To illuminate the night = the illustration of truth from good.
The light (there) illuminates not only the sight, but also their minds... This is meant by... that was the true light, which illuminates every man that Cometh into the world (). TCR 59:end.
Hence it is that they have no illumination when they are reading the Word.
Illuminate, because the light hath come... ().

It shall illuminate overagainst its faces () = from the Divine good of the Lord's Divine Human. To illuminate = the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord's Divine good; for this is what illuminates Heaven, and the Angels themselves there; also the Church and the men there who are in faith from good. The illumination thence is the illumination of the mind, whence come intelligence and wisdom in the truths and goods of faith. The mind is illuminated by means of the Word...

These are in the light of Heaven; thus in illumination from the Lord: but the former are... in the light of the world; thus in illumination from self. They who are illuminated from self, and not from the Lord, see falsity as truth, and evil as good.
This light with them is illuminated by the light of Heaven.
They with whom the internal spiritual man is open... are in... illumination from the Lord.
As these are solely in the light of the world, and in illumination thence, they believe in nature as Divine...
For the light of Heaven... illuminates the Intellectual of man...
Thus the higher degree acts from within into the exterior natural one, and illuminates it...
The candle was seen to be carried round about, and to illumine; and as it had not been snuffed, it illumined little.
The (spiritual) light inflows continually; and as it illumines, it also vivifies the understanding of man.
For, as the eye is illumined by the light of the natural sun, so the understanding is illumined by the light of the spiritual Sun; nor is it only illumined...
It illuminated better than if there had been windows at the sides.
Truths illuminate charity and its exercises. That they illuminate, the Lord teaches. Illustrated. -.
If the revelations were innumerable, they would not confuse, but illuminate...
These are never confused, but are illuminated...
Thus can Divine Truths be confirmed, to the illumination of the human mind...
It at once appears to those who are illuminated by the Lord...
To illumine the lamp () = to illustrate the understanding by means of Divine truth.
The illumination of the gentiles. Treated of.

Their first illumination is signified by, the Spirit of God moved upon the faces of the waters; and God said, Let there be light, and there was light. To move upon the faces of the waters = illustration.
God Jehovah who illuminates us (). To illuminate = to illustrate in truths.
Illumine Thy faces upon Thy servant (). To illumine the faces = to illustrate with Divine truth from Divine love. Explained. AE 412:3.
(Man thus) becomes more illumined and intelligent in the things of the Church.
